summary_paragraph: An elderly male with a history of alcohol abuse, COPD, atrial fibrillation, and prior CABG was admitted for acute shortness of breath and fever. He presented with septic physiology, including elevated lactate and hypotension, and imaging revealed multifocal pneumonia with a new cavitary lesion in the left lung, likely due to aspiration. He was treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics initially, then de-escalated to levofloxacin monotherapy as cultures returned negative. His condition improved rapidly with normalization of vitals, resolution of fever, and weaning off supplemental oxygen. He remained in atrial fibrillation but with controlled rates on diltiazem. He was discharged home on a five-day course of oral levofloxacin with instructions to follow up for a repeat chest X-ray in one week to monitor the cavitary lesion.
